Hi Diego —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we move toward a reserved commitment we wanted to start the sizing homework on our side and get your pre-sales intake so we can align on GPU mix and billing. I attached a small traffic snapshot (orchardai_traffic_snapshot.csv) and the SOW requirements PDF.

Quick context: OrchardAI is planning to move a mix of production-chat endpoints (customer-facing, low-latency) and an offline batch scoring job (nightly). We're evaluating a 12–18 month committed pool with burst headroom. We're sensitive to unit cost and are exploring quantized variants.

Can you confirm what fields you need completed in your template to give us a conservative fleet estimate? If it helps, here's our current quick summary:
- Average daily requests: 420k (chat + batch triggers)
- Peak concurrent chat sessions (observed): ~1,250 (5–10 min sessions)
- Median prompt tokens (chat): 80 tokens; median completion: 120 tokens
- Batch job: ~6M prompts/day, average prompt 60 tokens, average response 45 tokens, flexible latency (minutes)

If you can send the preflight template and a short list of clarifying Qs we’ll fill and return by EOD Friday.

Thanks —
Samira
Head of Platform Engineering
OrchardAI

Hi Samira —

Great summary, thanks. I’m attaching our preflight workbook (redwood_preflight_template.xlsx) — that’s the quickest path for us to generate a conservative committed sizing and a burst plan. A few clarifying questions to help us avoid back-and-forth:

1) Chat traffic shape and session model:
   - Are the 1,250 concurrent sessions evenly distributed across the day or concentrated in a 2–4 hour peak window?
   - Do sessions typically maintain an open KV-cache (multi-turn) over the 5–10 minute duration, or are they mostly single-turn (stateless)?

2) Prompt/response token distribution:
   - You listed median prompt 80 / completion 120 — can you provide 90th and 99th percentile token lengths for both prompt and completion? These drive KV cache sizing and p99 latency on long tails.

3) Model & quality targets:
   - Which model family and size are you targeting for chat (eg. LlamaX-13B quantized vs 34B fp16)? If undecided, we can run two scenarios.

4) Batch job characteristics:
   - Is the 6M prompts/day evenly batched across a maintenance window, or spread with smaller micro-batches?

5) SLA and outage tolerances:
   - Do you need a hard p99 latency SLA (e.g., 300ms for top-tier customers) or is graceful degradation (fallback to smaller model) acceptable for some traffic classes?

6) Security/compliance:
   - Any on-prem / VPC-only requirement or is hosted Dedicated acceptable?

If you can populate the template and drop the 90/99 token percentiles and the desired model target, we’ll run a quick estimator and aim to return a first-pass committed fleet break (GPU SKUs, baseline pool, burst buffer, and cost ranges) within 48 business hours.

Proposed next step: 30-min sizing call after you populate — I’m available Tue/Wed next week.

Diego
Senior Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

Hi Samira —

Thanks for the traffic snapshot and context. I’ve attached a partially completed preflight workbook (redwood_preflight_template.xlsx) with the sections we can prefill from your CSV and our assumptions highlighted in yellow. High-level notes from our side:

- Conservative sizing scenario (13B quantized primary, 34B fp16 fallback):
   • Baseline pool: 48 x A10G-equivalent (shared across chat and batch, session pooling enabled)
   • Burst buffer: additional 12 GPUs (25% burst) for 2–4 hour peak windows
   • Estimated committed monthly cost (net): $98k–$115k depending on sustained utilization and batching efficiencies

- Aggressive quality scenario (34B fp16 primary):
   • Baseline pool: 80 x A10G-equivalent (or 20 x 80GB-class GPUs depending on architecture)
   • Burst buffer: 20 GPUs; higher unit cost but lowers fallback risk

Open questions we highlighted in the workbook: 90/99 token percentiles, exact session affinity (cached kv per session), and whether batch can be fully shifted to a nightly window.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached workbook and add the 90/99 token percentiles + indicate session affinity checkboxes.
2) Confirm whether Orchard prefers a single-region us-west1 commit or a dual-region with DR (adds ~15% to cost).
3) Let us know if Tue 2026-09-13 10:00 PT works for the 30-min sizing call — meeting link: https://meet.redwood.ai/sizing/orchardai-20260913

If you’d like, Ben and I can run the estimator live on the call to show KU/tokens -> GPU mapping.

Regards,
